title: Analyzing non-infection-related health care utilization and health outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes during the COVID-19 pandemic: making use of individually linked statutory health insurance data and survey data
summary:
Existing studies have shown that the COVID-19 pandemic led, at least temporarily, to a decline in the utilization of health care services. The reasons for this decline may lie in a reduced supply of health care services (i.e., system-driven factors) or in a reduced demand for health care services (i.e., patient-side factors). However, it remains unclear whether there were changes in health care utilization among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) during the pandemic, what may have driven such changes, and whether and to what extent they resulted in adverse health consequences.
The aim of this study is to investigate changes in health care utilization and health outcomes during the pandemic. In doing so, the study examines whether these changes differ between individuals with and without T2DM and whether certain population subgroups were particularly affected. In addition, the study explores the role of fear of SARS-CoV-2 infection (as well as other factors) in health care utilization and missed or canceled appointments, and the potential health consequences thereof.
To address these objectives, a population-based observational study is conducted, in which routinely collected statutory health insurance data generated in the course of health care provision (secondary data) are linked with self-reported information collected through a survey (primary data) from a randomly selected subgroup of insured individuals.
The results of this study are intended to help identify potential gaps in health care provision and to inform improvements in health care delivery in future pandemics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Specific inclusion criteria (SHI population):

Source population:
Individuals insured with AOK Rheinland/Hamburg who were continuously insured from January 1, 2017, to March 31, 2020 (maximum gap of 30 days per year), and who were born in 1976 or earlier.
T2DM group:
All individuals from the source population with type 2 diabetes mellitus in 2017, identified using an established algorithm (WIdO 2025).
Potential controls:
All individuals from the source population without any diabetes diagnosis (no ICD-10 codes E10–E14 in any sector of care), without prescriptions for ATC A10 medications, and without participation in a disease management program (DMP; type 1 or type 2 diabetes) during the period 2017–2023.
Controls (matching):
1:1 matching to T2DM cases using exact matching based on year of birth, sex, and the quarter of the last day of insurance coverage (2020–2023).

Specific inclusion criteria (survey):

Potential survey participants:
Individuals from the T2DM group and the control group with continuous insurance coverage (maximum gap of 30 days) from January 1, 2017, up to the current time point.
Sample:
Random selection of n = 5,500 individuals each from the T2DM group and the control group, followed by postal invitation to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals with diabetes mellitus who cannot be clearly classified as having type 2 diabetes mellitus are excluded. This includes, in particular:

- Individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10)
- Individuals with other or unspecified types of diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E12–E14), if a clear classification as type 2 diabetes is not possible
- Individuals with inconsistent or non-classifiable diabetes diagnoses (e.g., concurrent coding of multiple diabetes types without a clear assignment within the hierarchical algorithm)

In addition, individuals are excluded if they are younger than 40 years of age or if they have interruptions in statutory health insurance coverage between 2017 and 2020 exceeding more than 30 days per calendar year
